newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia cuts refinancing rate to 42 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia cuts refinancing rate to 42 pct.

text.p: The Russian Central Bank said on Friday it was cutting its refinancing rate to 42 percent from 48 percent with effect from February 10.
It last changed the rate on December 2, cutting it to 48 percent from 60 percent.

The central bank does not actually lend any money through a refinancing facility based on the refinancing rate, but many commercial contracts and banking penalties are tied to the refinancing rate which has an important signal effect in the economy.
The rate cut follows news that the monthly inflation rate jumped to 2.3 percent in January from 1.4 percent in December.
Economists said the rise in January was seasonal, reflecting administered price rises at the start of the year, and inflation was likely to slow again to around 1.5 percent in February.
Treasury bill yields have been falling in recent months, and are now just above 30 percent.
The central bank also changed the rates on its Lombard facility, and the period terms of the Lombard loans.
From February 10 it will charge an annual rate of 24 percent on loans from three to seven days, the same rate as now applies to seven-day loans.
The rate on 8-14 day loans will be 33 percent instead of 36 percent on 14-day loans, and the rate on 15-30 day loans will be 42 percent instead of 48 percent.
